chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Refusing to unload boxcars in the Oakland port company
summary: Placed in a port company in Oakland, Collins refused boxcar duty, was made to wash a hundred windows on Thanksgiving, and was transferred to a band camp.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: didn't understand the type of company I was in, which didn't mean too much to me any way because I assumed that they had a band and that I would be in the band.

So they called me up one morning and marched me down to a freight yard where there were 14 freight cars to be unloaded, and he was calling off squads of 10 and he called me off and I said, no, you have nine. You don't have 10 this time. So the guy said, fine, so it's all right with me. So we went back to camp and they called me into the office, and the commanding officer said, well you refused to do this work today. And I said, yes. He said, why. I said, well if you'll look at my record you'll see that I'm a musician and I've always -- ever since I've been in the army this is all I have done. I don't know anything about unloading any box cars. Can you imagine this.

But any way, he made me wash every window on Thanksgiving Day. I washed every window in that mess hall, I think, which -- I think it was 100 windows. But I went to the special service officer then. I did the duty and then I went to the special service officer and I told him. And I'm wondering how did I get in a company like this. And he sent for my records and he saw what was happening, so he transferred me to another camp in Oakland, and in the band was Benny Green, and you know, this was -- I'm home free now.
But this is what they can do to you if you don't
stand up for yourself. And Lester wouldn't.
